keyTakeaways: A client Diwali greeting with an offer attached stops being a greeting: TRAI's 2018 regulations define commercial communication by whether the primary purpose is to advertise or solicit business.

51.8% of the 33,007 recorded views of SubhSandesh pages open on a phone and 44.3% of creators add a password (measured 2026-08-19) — right for a private note, wrong for a client greeting.

faqs.question: Should I send Diwali wishes to clients and customers at all?
faqs.answer: Only if you can send it without an offer attached and without spraying it at people who do not observe Diwali. If your book is 10–50 accounts, the account owner sending individually is better than any company-wide send; if you are mid-dispute or chasing an overdue invoice with that client, send nothing.

faqs.question: Can I add a Diwali offer or discount code to the greeting?
faqs.answer: You can, but it stops being a greeting. TRAI's 2018 regulations define commercial communication by whether the primary purpose is to inform about, advertise or solicit business, so the offer is what moves your message into that category and into the consent, header and content-template requirements around it.

faqs.question: Is it okay to send a Diwali message on WhatsApp to my customer list?
faqs.answer: Not as a bulk broadcast to numbers that never opted in. WhatsApp sits outside TRAI's telecom regulation but has its own opt-in requirement, and Diwali blasts to cold numbers get reported, which damages your sender quality for the messages you actually need to deliver.

faqs.question: What do I send to customers who do not celebrate Diwali?
faqs.answer: A festival-neutral line — "wishing you a warm festive season and a good close to the year" — for the unsegmented part of your list. Almost no CRM stores religion, and guessing it from a name is both unreliable and a bad look, so neutral wording is the honest default for a large list.

faqs.question: Can I send a Diwali gift to a client who works for a government department?
faqs.answer: Generally no. Rule 13 of the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 bars a Government servant from accepting a gift from anyone other than a near relative or personal friend with no official dealings, and a vendor has official dealings by definition. A greeting with no monetary value avoids the problem entirely.

faqs.question: What is the gift value limit for Indian government officers?
faqs.answer: Under Rule 13, gifts on occasions such as weddings, anniversaries, funerals or religious functions must be reported above ₹25,000 for a Group A officer, ₹15,000 for Group B and ₹7,500 for Group C — and even then only from relatives or friends with no official dealings. In any other case, sanction is needed above ₹1,500 (Group A or B) or ₹500 (Group C or D).

faqs.question: When should I send Diwali wishes to clients in 2026?
faqs.answer: Friday 6 November 2026, before roughly 4pm IST. Diwali falls on Sunday 8 November 2026 and the five-day festival runs 6–10 November, so Friday 6 and the Monday–Tuesday of 9–10 November are the only ordinary working days inside it.

faqs.question: Should the greeting come from the company or from the account manager?
faqs.answer: From the account manager wherever the relationship is real, because a reply then lands with a human instead of a no-reply inbox. Reserve the company-signed version for the long tail of customers nobody owns individually.

faqs.question: How long should a corporate Diwali message to a client be?
faqs.answer: Twenty to thirty-five words. A greeting that runs longer starts justifying itself, and the justification is what makes it read like marketing rather than goodwill.

faqs.question: Does SubhSandesh have a Diwali template for client greetings?
faqs.answer: No. Diwali is not one of the 13 page types among the 2,739 pages created since 2026-03-12 (measured 2026-08-19); the festival pages that exist today are Holi and Eid Mubarak. For a client greeting this Diwali, a plain email from the account owner is the honest recommendation.

faqs.question: Should I password-protect a greeting page I send to a client?
faqs.answer: No. 44.3% of SubhSandesh creators password-protect a page before sharing it (1,213 of 2,739, measured 2026-08-19), which suits a private message and not a client greeting — a password turns a wish into a task, and a client will not do it.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Diwali Wishes for Clients and Customers: Where the Line Sits

Send it as a greeting and nothing else — no offer, no discount code, no product mention — and send it to named people rather than to a list. On SubhSandesh, 2,739 personalised pages have been created since 2026-03-12 across 13 page types, and 51.8% of the 33,007 recorded views are opened on a phone (17,101 of 33,007, measured 2026-08-19). That is the reading condition: a client sees your Diwali wish on a phone, between two other messages, and decides in a second whether it is personal or bulk.

Diwali 2026 falls on Sunday 8 November, the five-day festival runs 6–10 November, and the working days around it are Friday 6 and Monday–Tuesday 9–10 November. Below: the wording, whether to send at all, the gift rules that make a greeting safer than a hamper, channel choice, and timing.

## What separates a client Diwali greeting from a Diwali campaign

A client Diwali greeting is a message whose only purpose is to mark the festival and thank the recipient. No offer, no product, no landing page, no call to action.

That distinction is not stylistic. The [Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference Regulations, 2018](https://www.trai.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-09/RegulationUcc19072018.pdf) define "commercial communication" as any voice call or message using telecommunication services "where the primary purpose is to inform about or advertise or solicit business for" goods or services, or a supplier of them.

A wish with nothing to sell does not meet that test. A wish carrying "20% off till 10 November" does.

The same regulation defines a "promotional message" as commercial communication for which the sender has taken no explicit consent from the recipient. So appending an offer does two things at once: it changes what your message is, and it pulls a festival greeting into a regime of registered headers, registered content templates and customer preferences — including preferences customers may set by time band and type of day.

Read the scope narrowly: that regulation governs calls and messages over telecom networks, so in practice SMS and voice. WhatsApp sits outside it under the platform's own opt-in rules, so "TRAI does not cover it" is not "you may broadcast freely."

## Four wordings that work when the sender is a company

Each of these is 20–35 words, because a greeting that runs longer starts arguing for itself.

### 1. The plain observance line

*"Wishing you and your team a bright Diwali. Thank you for a good year of working together."* Suits any client, any industry, any list size.

It works because it claims nothing and asks for nothing, which is exactly what makes it readable as a greeting rather than an ad. Avoid adding your tagline underneath — a tagline is a product mention.

### 2. The thank-you with a specific reason

*"Happy Diwali. Thank you for backing the migration in June — it was the hardest thing we shipped this year."* Suits your top 10–30 accounts, where you can name a real event.

Specificity is the whole value. A [dyadic study of 100 buyer–seller pairs](http://sajms.iurc.edu.pk//issues/2020b/SAJMS3.pdf) found a seller's relationship investments predicted the customer's gratitude strongly (β = 0.572) but had no significant direct effect on reciprocity (β = 0.084) — the return only arrives via the customer actually feeling grateful, which a generic thanks does not achieve.

### 3. The neutral line for a mixed list

*"Wishing you a warm festive season and a good close to the year."* Suits a customer list spanning religions, regions and countries, where a Diwali-specific line will reach people who do not observe it. It reads slightly flatter, and that is the trade. Do not use it for a client you know celebrates — they will notice the hedge.

### 4. The account owner's personal note

*"Happy Diwali, Meera. Hope you get a few days off — talk in the week of the 16th."* Suits named contacts you actually speak to, sent from that person's own address or number. This is the only version that survives a reply, because a reply lands with a human rather than in a no-reply inbox.

## Should this go to your whole customer list, or to one account owner?

For a B2B book of 10–50 accounts, do not send a blast at all. The account owner sends individually, from their own address, and the whole exercise costs an afternoon.

Above roughly 200 accounts a personal note per client stops being real, so the honest options narrow to a plainly-worded company greeting or nothing. The failure mode people skip is segmentation: almost no CRM stores a contact's religion, and inferring it from a name is both unreliable and a bad look. A Diwali blast to an unsegmented customer list therefore reaches Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Parsi and non-observant customers as well as Hindu, Jain and Sikh ones who do celebrate.

That argues for either a festival-neutral line, or a targeted send only to accounts where you have direct evidence: a client who wished you first, or a company that closed for Diwali last year.

## Gift or greeting: what India's gift rules actually restrict

A greeting is compliant almost everywhere a hamper is not, and that is the strongest practical argument for sending words rather than sweets.

Rule 13 of the [Central Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1964](https://dopt.gov.in/sites/default/files/CCS_Conduct_Rules_1964_Updated_27Feb15_0.pdf) says no Government servant shall accept any gift except as the rules allow, and defines "gift" to include free transport, boarding, lodging or any other pecuniary advantage from anyone other than a near relative or a personal friend **having no official dealings** with them. A vendor has official dealings by definition.

The rule's festival carve-out does not rescue you either. It permits gifts on occasions such as weddings, anniversaries, funerals or religious functions — but only from near relatives or personal friends with no official dealings, and only with a report to Government above ₹25,000 for a Group A officer, ₹15,000 for Group B and ₹7,500 for Group C. In any other case the officer needs sanction above ₹1,500 (Group A or B) or ₹500 (Group C or D).

Private companies are outside that rule but many set their own ceilings. A [survey of 14 UK airline marketers](http://bura.brunel.ac.uk/bitstream/2438/1284/3/Corporate%2bgifts-1.pdf) (67% response rate) found gift value treated as the single factor separating a gift from a bribe, with guardrails cited as "token value" or "less than £30".

Ask procurement before couriering anything. Nobody has had to ask before sending a sentence.

## Email, WhatsApp Business, a link, or a printed card

The comparison below is about consent and effort, not aesthetics. Only the last column is data we hold ourselves.

| Option | Consent basis you need | Effort for 100 clients | SubhSandesh data (2026-08-19) |
|---|---|---|---|
| One-to-one email from the account owner | Existing business contact, no bulk consent | About 3–4 hours of one person's day | Not measured — we do not send email |
| Bulk email to the whole customer list | Working unsubscribe plus current list hygiene | Under an hour once segmented | Not measured |
| WhatsApp Business broadcast | Per-number opt-in under the platform's rules | Minutes, and spam reports hit sender quality | Not measured |
| A shareable greeting page link | None beyond the channel carrying the link | 6.9 hours median between first save and last edit (n=914) | 51.8% of 33,007 views open on a phone |
| Printed card by courier | None, but you need current postal addresses | 5–7 working days plus address cleanup | Not measured |

The two low-consent-risk options are the personal email and a link; the link is the only one needing nothing installed.

One warning specific to a shared page: 44.3% of SubhSandesh creators password-protect their page before sharing it (1,213 of 2,739, measured 2026-08-19). That is right for a private message and wrong for a client greeting — a password on a Diwali wish is a task, and a client will not do it.

## Timing a client greeting when Diwali 2026 falls on a Sunday

Send on Friday 6 November 2026, before about 4pm IST. Diwali is Sunday 8 November, offices are already thinning by Friday afternoon, and a business-hours send on the Sunday itself lands in a phone that is being used for family, not work.

The five-day festival runs 6–10 November 2026, so the only ordinary working days inside it are Friday 6 and the Monday and Tuesday of 9–10 November, and many Indian offices close for at least one of those. A greeting arriving on Wednesday 11 November reads as an afterthought.

Give yourself lead time on the artefact, not the send. Our median gap between a page's first save and its last edit is 6.9 hours, sampled on /love-gf across n=914 pages (measured 2026-08-19) — people write, leave, then fix the wording. Assume the same for anything a client reads.

## When a client Diwali greeting is the wrong move

Skip it entirely if you are mid-dispute, mid-renewal negotiation, or chasing an overdue invoice. A festival wish arriving while your collections email sits unanswered reads as pressure dressed as warmth.

Skip it too if the only version you can get signed off has the offer in it. [B2B relationship quality — trust, commitment and satisfaction together](http://www.iiisci.org/Journal/CV$/sci/pdfs/HSA292TS.pdf) explained 56% of the variance in customer loyalty across 310 business customers of Egyptian shipping services, and none of those three is helped by a wish that turns out to be an ad.

Sending nothing costs you nothing. Sending an ad in a diya-shaped wrapper costs you a little trust.

And be honest about the artefact. SubhSandesh has no Diwali template today — Diwali is not one of the 13 page types among those 2,739 created pages, and the [festival pages that exist](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) are the [Holi greeting page](https://subhsandesh.in/holi) and the [Eid Mubarak page](https://subhsandesh.in/eid-mubarak). For a client greeting this Diwali, a plain email from the account owner beats a page built on the wrong festival's design.

## Sources

- [Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference Regulations, 2018](https://www.trai.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-09/RegulationUcc19072018.pdf) — Telecom Regulatory Authority of India, 19 July 2018.
- [Central Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1964](https://dopt.gov.in/sites/default/files/CCS_Conduct_Rules_1964_Updated_27Feb15_0.pdf) — Department of Personnel & Training, updated 27 February 2015.
- [Promoting Business with Corporate Gifts — Major Issues and Empirical Evidence](http://bura.brunel.ac.uk/bitstream/2438/1284/3/Corporate%2bgifts-1.pdf) — Ying Fan, *Corporate Communications: An International Journal*, 2006.
- [Relationship Quality as Predictor of B2B Customer Loyalty](http://www.iiisci.org/Journal/CV$/sci/pdfs/HSA292TS.pdf) — Shaimaa S. B. Ahmed Doma, *Journal of Systemics, Cybernetics and Informatics*, 2013.
- [Interpersonal Relationship Marketing: Reciprocity in Buyer-Seller Dyad with Customer Gratitude as Mediator](http://sajms.iurc.edu.pk//issues/2020b/SAJMS3.pdf) — *South Asian Journal of Management Sciences*, 2020.

auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine has a reason to cite this because it is the only page on the query that answers the compliance and consent half of the question from primary text — TRAI's definition of "commercial communication" and the actual ₹1,500/₹500 ceilings in Rule 13 of the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 — instead of listing 30 to 101 wishes, and because it says plainly that some businesses should send nothing. Three caveats: the first-party column of the comparison table only carries values on two of five rows, because SubhSandesh measures its own shared pages and not anyone's email or WhatsApp sends; the platform-wide figures (51.8% mobile, 44.3% password, 6.9-hour edit gap) are about making and sharing a greeting rather than about Diwali, and would fit any other post in this batch, so they support the argument without being unique to it; and there is no Diwali-specific first-party fact at all, which the post states rather than papers over. TRAI is cited as regulatory text, not as a subscriber statistic, so the batch's one-context-statistic budget is untouched. Domain authority here is far below the reward platforms and wishes farms holding the SERP, so treat this as a months-long play, not weeks.
